subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: one strong member doing everything [Pitfall]
passage: Coach's note, Harsha. Uday built the whole robot himself: wiring, code, chassis. The team watched. When teammates offered to help, he said it was quicker if he did it, and they let him. On competition day he was ill and stayed home. The other three stood at the table. They could not start the robot, and they could not answer the judges' questions about the sensors. We withdrew before the first run. I sat with the team afterwards and told them it was not about blame, and later I called Uday to say the same. Next entry, I have asked him to teach one part to each teammate before the event, and each of them to explain it back to the group.

qa.a: Uday built the whole robot himself.

qa.q: How might Uday's teammates have felt standing at the table?
qa.a: They were probably helpless and embarrassed, since they could not start the robot or answer the judges' questions.

qa.q: What could the team do differently next time?
qa.a: They could share tasks and teach each teammate a part in advance, so anyone can run the robot and explain it.

qa.q: How might Uday feel when he hears what happened?
qa.a: Uday may feel guilty and disappointed that his illness left the team stuck, though Harsha tells him it is not about blame.

grounding: A gifted teen builds the whole project alone because it is quicker, and when he falls ill on the day, teammates cannot operate or explain it.

subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: one strong member doing everything [Pitfall]
passage:
Friday, 9 pm
Today was the district science fair and it was a disaster.
Nilesh built our whole solar tracker himself over the last month. Whenever I offered to help, he said, "It's faster if I do it, Lakshmi." It was faster. So Farhan and I made the poster, and that's all.
This morning his mother called: Nilesh had a high fever and wasn't coming. Farhan and I stood next to a machine we had never switched on. The first judge asked why the panel turns toward the light. I said, "Because of the sensors?" She asked, "Which sensors?" I didn't know. Farhan tried to start it and pressed the wrong switch. The panel just sat there.
I'm not even angry at Nilesh. I'm angry at us for letting it happen. Next project, everyone learns everything, at least once.
Lakshmi

qa.q: What did Nilesh say when offered help?
qa.a: It's faster if I do it, Lakshmi.

qa.q: How does Lakshmi feel at the end of the day?
qa.a: Lakshmi feels frustrated, angry at the team more than at Nilesh for letting one person hold all the knowledge.

qa.q: What would you change first for the next project?
qa.a: Have each member build, run and explain every part at least once, with the builder teaching as they go.

qa.q: How might Nilesh feel hearing about the fair?
qa.a: Nilesh, stuck at home with fever, may feel guilty and helpless that the project he built couldn't be shown without him.

grounding: Shows a gifted teen building the whole project alone, so when he falls ill on the day the teammates cannot run or explain it.

passage:
Nazia: Mohit where are you?? we're up in 40 min
Mohit: sorry. high fever. mom won't let me go 🤒
Nazia: ok ok get well. but how do I start the robot
Mohit: blue switch under the base, then hold reset for 3 sec, then press A on the remote
Nazia: there's no blue switch
Mohit: it's under the battery holder. you have to lift it
Nazia: found it. it's beeping??
Mohit: that means the sensors aren't calibrated. you need to run the calibration file from my laptop
Nazia: your laptop is at your house Mohit 😰
Mohit: oh no
Nazia: the judges are asking me what the tuning values do
Mohit: that's hard to explain on chat
Nazia: I'm going to tell them the truth. one person built this and the rest of us don't know how it works
Mohit: I'm really sorry. I thought it was quicker if I did it all myself

qa.a: The laptop is at Mohit's house.

qa.q: How is Nazia feeling as the minutes pass?
qa.a: Nazia grows anxious and frustrated, unable to start the robot or answer the judges without Mohit.

qa.q: What could the team have done weeks earlier?
qa.a: Mohit could have taught each teammate to start, calibrate and explain the robot, with the steps written down and the files shared, so anyone could run it.

qa.q: What is it like for Mohit to follow the chat from home?
qa.a: Mohit feels helpless and sorry, watching the team struggle and realising doing it all alone was not quicker after all.

grounding: Illustrates a strong member who built everything alone falling ill on the day, leaving a teammate unable to operate or explain the robot.
